statement.essentials: Surgeons divide the gland into five parts, called levels, so that an operation can be described by what it removes.
statement.anatomy: The European Salivary Gland Society divides the parotid into five levels: I (lateral superior), II (lateral inferior), III (deep inferior), IV (deep superior) and V (accessory). Lateral and deep are set by the plane of the facial nerve; superior and inferior by where the main trunk divides into its temporofacial and cervicofacial branches.
statement.clinical: Parotidectomies are classified by the levels removed and the extra-parotid structures ablated. Extracapsular dissection is classed separately: it avoids facial nerve dissection and removes less than one level, so level I or II is recorded only to show where the tumour lay.

limitations: A consensus classification, not a measurement. The model places the superior/inferior boundary through the buccal branch between the temporofacial and cervicofacial territories; the primary paper’s full text was not available, so this boundary is the project’s reading of the secondary description.
